description: §14.8.9 — laundering shape: `.map` over tagged rows returning the protected column (`rows.map(r => r.passwordHash)`) is E-PROTECT-006 — the array holds bare strings, no row descriptor survives.
rationale: §14.8.9: every compiler-emitted client-egress serializer "SHALL strip, by construction, every column whose provenance origin is a `protect=` field … keys on the column's resolved source `(table, column)` origin". The runtime strip reads a descriptor the ROW carries; a value extracted from the row carries none, so before S441 (g-protected-column-escapes-redaction-as-scalar) this shape compiled at exit 0 and shipped the column — MEASURED, HTTP 200 body "SECRET-HASH-123" for the plain scalar — while I-PROTECT-STRIP-001 claimed it had been stripped. The §14.8.9 provenance flow (compiler/src/codegen/protect-flow.ts) now rejects it at compile time as E-PROTECT-006, and the info no longer fires because nothing was stripped. Goes RED against the pre-S441 emitter (no E-PROTECT-006 existed).
